observations: Matched contact sheets cover grasp, lift, first snip, second snip, withdrawal, scissor opening, extraction and hold. Large-scale attachment/stretching and two snips occur in both; this is not proof of tissue realism.
At step 750 the candidate and baseline have visibly different local attachment/separation geometry. The motion plot shows different grasper opening and blade-load trajectories.

Both complete videos preserve all 1111 states. Motion statistics read every state; visual inspection uses the listed matched contact sheets and full-trajectory plot, not an assertion that every pixel of every frame was manually reviewed.
The hold-stage tumor RMS speed peak is 0.1596 vs 1.0536 mm/s; candidate non-cutting overlap is 0.0784 vs 0.0250 mm. Neither statistic alone establishes clinical realism.
Acceptance remains false; no default adoption. The scripted release only opens scissors.

Matched sheets show maintained grasp/lift, two snips and extraction in both recordings. Local neck/cut shapes and grasper opening differ during snips; whole-trajectory plot shows an appreciable first-snip jaw-gap difference.

Baseline/candidate first-snip mean jaw gap: 3.0703 / 1.9552 mm. Second-snip tumor RMS speed peak: 32.8386 / 27.6239 mm/s; hold peak: 0.7853 / 0.1620 mm/s. These are descriptive differences, not realism pass criteria.
Fresh baselines from the two experiment sequences also differ: first-snip mean jaw gap 2.0895 vs 3.0703 mm. No cause for this repeat variability is established.
